title: Point-Free Pipelines with B and W
description: Use the Warbler W and Bluebird B to compose functions in point-free style without naming the input parameter.

steps.description: Import reduce, define B and W, and look at the point-full function square_then_add_one_v1(x) that names x explicitly.
Build square = W(lambda x: lambda y: x * y) and compose it with add_one via B(add_one)(square) without naming the input parameter, then test on 5 and 3.

steps.question: In process = pipeline(replace, str.lower, str.strip), in what order do the three string functions run on '  Hello World  '?
steps.answer: Because B(a)(b)(x) computes a(b(x)), the rightmost function str.strip runs first, then str.lower, and finally replace(' ', '_'), producing 'hello_world'.

steps.description: Fold B across multiple functions with reduce in pipeline and run process('  Hello World  ') to print 'hello_world'.
Step through process('  Hello World  ') to see str.strip, str.lower, and replace execute from right to left.
